question: For $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{bmatrix},\quad B=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{bmatrix},$$ calculate $AB$ and $BA$. What conclusion can you draw about matrix multiplication?
explanation:
Product $AB$
$$AB=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{bmatrix}$$
Product $BA$
$$BA=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}$$
Comparison
Since $AB\neq BA$, matrix multiplication is not commutative in general.

options.C: $AB=BA=I_2$; matrix multiplication is commutative for square matrices.
options.D: $AB=\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{bmatrix}$ and $BA=\begin{bmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}$; hence matrix multiplication is not commutative in general.
